title: Product Unavailable Details
description: Recommended details shape for PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE when a seller refuses to book or grow packages because one or more of them asks for more than the seller can deliver. Applies to buy_products, accept_proposal, control_media_buy, and the 3.x create_media_buy and update_media_buy facades. A seller that uses this shape MUST include an entry for every package it refuses, so a buyer can correct the whole request in one resubmission. It MAY also list packages that fit, with their headroom, so the buyer can move budget onto them. A package absent from packages carries no availability claim. Every figure is a snapshot of the seller's state when it refused, never a hold or reservation. When the refusal arrives as the terminal error of an async task that ends in failed, the same details MUST appear on that task's errors[] entry. The complete details travel on the payload errors[] entry; a transport-envelope adcp_error copy, which buyers discard above 4096 bytes, carries them only when the whole error fits. error.recovery is transient only when every unavailable entry has reason forecast_unavailable; otherwise it is correctable. A seller that refuses before any write SHOULD set mutation_outcome not_applied; a buyer changes the request only after the refusal is known to have committed nothing.

packages.description: Per-package availability. At most one entry per package; entry order carries no meaning. Every entry locates its package by package_field, package_id, or both. Each entry's bookable assumes every other package in the request stays as requested; packages that draw on the same inventory can share headroom, so moving budget onto several of them at once can still be refused.

package_field.description: JSONPath-lite locator of the package's row, using the same convention as error.field: purchases[i] on buy_products, packages[i] on create_media_buy, update_media_buy and control_media_buy, and new_packages[i] on update_media_buy. The index is the submitted request row, never a readback array index. On accept_proposal, whose request carries no package rows, it is rooted at the committed proposal: commercial_terms.purchases[i]. Omit when the package has no such row, as for an existing package listed only for its headroom, which package_id then identifies; do not fabricate an index. Every entry carries package_field, package_id, or both.

package_id.description: Seller-assigned ID of the package when it already exists, as on an update_media_buy packages[] row, a control_media_buy row, or an existing package listed for its headroom. Absent for a package the request would create.

product_id.description: Product of the package, echoed from the request or the committed proposal.

enumDescriptions.impressions: Ad-server or first-party delivery count, as the forecastable metric impressions.
enumDescriptions.viewable_impressions: Impressions meeting the viewability threshold, as viewability.viewable_impressions on a forecast point. Typical for a vcpm pricing option.
enumDescriptions.measured_impressions: Impressions as counted by the third-party measurement provider, as the forecastable metric measured_impressions.
enumDescriptions.clicks: Clicks, as the forecastable metric clicks.
enumDescriptions.views: Views at the publisher-defined threshold, as the forecastable metric views.
enumDescriptions.completed_views: Video or audio completions, as the forecastable metric completed_views.
enumDescriptions.grps: Gross Rating Points, as the forecastable metric grps. The only fractional unit.
enumDescriptions.plays: DOOH or broadcast plays before any impression multiplier, as the forecastable metric plays.
enumDescriptions.downloads: Podcast downloads, as the forecastable metric downloads.

unit.description: Delivery unit that requested, available and bookable are counted in, named as in forecasts. Never a money unit; money figures belong in max_budget, which carries a currency and a pricing option. A package that states only a budget is counted in the delivery unit of its pricing option: impressions for cpm, viewable_impressions for vcpm, clicks for cpc, completed_views for cpcv, views for cpv, grps for cpp. When no delivery unit applies, as with flat_rate or time pricing, or when the seller cannot count the package in one, omit unit, requested, available and bookable.

requested.description: What the package asks for, in unit: its goal when it states one in unit; otherwise, for a package with a fixed allocation priced at a positive fixed_price, the quantity its budget buys at that price (per 1,000 for cpm and vcpm), rounded down. Sellers MUST NOT derive it from a floor_price, price_guidance, bid, or zero fixed_price, which are not rates the budget is guaranteed to buy at, and MUST NOT derive it from a seller-optimized package budget, which is a ceiling rather than an allocation; such a package without a goal in unit omits requested. On an increase through control_media_buy or update_media_buy, the resulting package total, not the increment. On an entry listed for headroom, the package's current or requested quantity. A whole number for every unit except grps.

available.description: Advisory forecast of what the package can deliver, in unit, for its targeting and flight. It carries the same uncertainty as a forecast and is not the booking limit; bookable is. Absent when availability could not be determined, or when the seller withholds it. Sellers MAY round or coarsen it.

bookable.description: The most the seller will accept for this package right now, in unit, as a package total with its other terms unchanged. It may exceed available.mid, for a seller that books above its forecast. A resubmission at or below bookable can still be refused if inventory moved after this response. Sellers SHOULD include it on every entry they refuse for over_forecast, even when they omit or coarsen available. A seller that rounds it MUST round down. 0 means nothing can be booked. A whole number for every unit except grps.

max_budget.description: The largest package budget that fits within bookable at the fixed_price of pricing_option_id (per 1,000 for cpm and vcpm), rounded down to the currency's minor unit, so the buyer does not have to back-calculate from the rate. On an entry listed for headroom, the budget the package could grow to. Same amount and currency shape as total_budget. A seller that rounds it MUST round down. Present only for a package with a fixed allocation priced at a positive fixed_price; absent for auction pricing (floor_price or price_guidance only), for flat_rate or time pricing, and for a package in seller-optimized allocation, whose package budget is a ceiling rather than an allocation.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. The currency of the package budget.

pricing_option_id.description: Pricing option the amount was computed at, normally the package's selected pricing option. A buyer MUST NOT apply the amount to a package priced at a different option.

availability_status.description: unavailable: the seller refuses the package as requested. available: the package as requested fits, with requested at or below bookable, and the entry reports its headroom.

enumDescriptions.over_forecast: The package asks for more than bookable. Recovery: correctable. Reduce the package to bookable or max_budget, move the difference to packages listed with headroom, or choose another product.
enumDescriptions.not_forecastable: The seller cannot forecast this goal or targeting, so it will not book it. Resubmitting the package unchanged is refused again. Recovery: correctable. Change the goal unit or targeting to one the seller can forecast, or choose another product.
enumDescriptions.forecast_unavailable: The seller's forecast timed out or errored. The request may book once forecasting recovers. Recovery: transient. After a synchronous refusal the key was released, so resend the same request with the same idempotency_key after error.retry_after, or with backoff. After a submitted task ended in failed, the same key only replays the original submitted response, so resend it as a new request with a new idempotency_key once the failure is known to have committed nothing.

reason.description: Why the seller refuses the package. Present on every unavailable entry; absent on available entries.
